STATES.TITLE: States
STATES.SUBTITLE: Toggle tracked character states and trigger their actions.
STATES.NAME: State
STATES.MANA_LEAK_MESSAGE: loses {value} MP or gains 1 spell slot.

SURPRISED.NAME: Surprised
SURPRISED.DESCRIPTION: At the start of combat, a creature may ambush another. If the creature is surprised, it cannot act during the first round of combat.

STUNNED.NAME: Stunned
STUNNED.DESCRIPTION: A stunned creature may be unconscious, dazed, or disoriented. In all cases, it is unable to act and becomes an easier target; its enemies gain Advantage on their attack tests.

DESTABILIZED.NAME: Destabilized
DESTABILIZED.DESCRIPTION: A destabilized creature suffers Disadvantage on its attack tests.

SLOWED.NAME: Slowed
SLOWED.DESCRIPTION: A slowed creature loses half of its movement speed, but its maximum stays the same. For example, if you have 12 m of movement speed, you lose 6 m. This also means it still costs you 6 m to stand up if you are prone, not 3 m.

PRONE.NAME: Prone
PRONE.DESCRIPTION: A prone creature suffers a -3 penalty to precision and -3 DEF until it stands up.

WEAKENED.NAME: Weakened
WEAKENED.DESCRIPTION: A weakened creature suffers Disadvantage on all its tests.

FEAR.NAME: Frightened
FEAR.DESCRIPTION: The creature’s first action is to move away from the source of fear. In addition, it must succeed on an INS attribute test with complex difficulty if it wishes to attack the source of fear.

BLINDED.NAME: Blinded
BLINDED.DESCRIPTION: A blinded creature suffers Disadvantage on PER attribute tests, a -3 penalty to DEF, and follows the attacking blind rule for its attack tests.

DEAF.NAME: Deafened
DEAF.DESCRIPTION: A deaf creature can no longer hear or make PER tests related to hearing.

BLEEDING.NAME: Bleeding
BLEEDING.DESCRIPTION: The creature bleeds for 1d6 rounds. At the start of its turn, it suffers 2 DM.

PAIN.NAME: Pain
PAIN.DESCRIPTION: A creature in pain may either move or use its action on its turn.

IMMOBILIZED.NAME: Immobilized
IMMOBILIZED.DESCRIPTION: An immobilized creature has its movement speed reduced to 0.

GRAVE_WOUND.NAME: Grave Wound
GRAVE_WOUND.DESCRIPTION: A creature suffering a grave wound has its maximum HP reduced by 3, starting from 12. Example: with 1 grave wound, the maximum possible HP is 9. This state can stack and does not disappear at the end of combat; it can only be healed by a SAV attribute test or by a skill that specifically mentions this state.

NECROSIS.NAME: Necrosis
NECROSIS.DESCRIPTION: Skills that would heal the creature are reduced by half.

BURN.NAME: Burn
BURN.DESCRIPTION: A creature suffering the burn state rolls 1d6; on 5+, it catches fire, then rolls 1d6 at the start of each turn. 1–2: the burn ends. 3–5: the creature suffers 3 fire DM. 6: the creature suffers 6 fire DM.

FROZEN.NAME: Frozen
FROZEN.DESCRIPTION: A creature suffering the frozen state rolls 1d6; on 5+, it gains 1 frost value. A creature with at least 1 frost value is unable to act except to try to break free. As an action, it makes a STR attribute test and loses 1 frost value for each success.

SHOCK.NAME: Shock
SHOCK.DESCRIPTION: A creature in shock has all its saves worsened by 1.

POISONED.NAME: Poisoned
POISONED.DESCRIPTION: A poisoned creature suffers 1d6 acid DM at the start of its turn for as long as the effect lasts. This effect is stackable.

MANA_LEAK.NAME: Mana Leak
MANA_LEAK.DESCRIPTION: A creature in the mana leak state loses 1d6 MP or gains 1 spell slot at the start of its turn.

SILENCED.NAME: Silenced
SILENCED.DESCRIPTION: A silenced creature can no longer speak or cast spells.

MADNESS.NAME: Madness
MADNESS.DESCRIPTION: A creature in the madness state rolls 1d6 to determine its first action of the turn. 1 or 2: the creature moves randomly. 3 or 4: the creature remains still and skips its turn. 5 or 6: the creature attacks the nearest creature.

CHARMED.NAME: Charmed
CHARMED.DESCRIPTION: A charmed creature acts as best it can to please the caster. In combat, it prioritizes defending the caster against any creature that attacks them.

REACTION.NAME: Reaction
REACTION.DESCRIPTION: A reaction is a technique triggered at any point during the round by spending a reaction action. It is added on top of another key.

OPPOSITION.NAME: Opposition
OPPOSITION.DESCRIPTION: An opposition replaces a classic test with a progress track opposing the characters. The first side to reach the objective wins the opposition. The objective may be fixed, such as difficulty 3, or duration-based, such as after 3 rounds the side with the most successes wins. This key is added on top of another key. If the opposition happens during an attack, after each test, the side that is furthest ahead on the progress track deals its DM to the other.

RECHARGE.NAME: Recharge
RECHARGE.DESCRIPTION: Recharge, 1 use. The technique can only be used once, then recharges only when the condition chosen and approved by the GM is fulfilled. The listed cost starts at -1 XP: adjust it between -1 and -4 XP depending on the approved restriction. Examples: short rest, eating or drinking, concentrating for 1 minute, end of any combat (-1); once per day, at night, sleeping at least 1 hour, after a suitable successful attribute test (-2); strong emotion, narrative trigger, defeating a significant opponent, risky action defined by the GM (-3); end of a story arc or chapter, after a serious wound, at a specific place, after a material or narrative sacrifice (-4).

CHANNELING.NAME: Channeling
CHANNELING.DESCRIPTION: A channeled technique uses a progress track with difficulty 5, 7, and 9. As long as you dedicate your actions to this technique, make the usual tests and fill the progress track according to your successes. Each objective reached increases the technique power by 2. After 3 rounds, or if you move or use a reaction for another purpose, the channeling ends.
